spec_features.spec_quote: terminates on `submit`, on an empty (no-tool-call) assistant turn, on error, or at `max_steps`
spec_features.evidence: agent.py run_agent loop: `for step_idx in range(task.max_steps):` with an `else: transcript.stop_reason = "max_steps"` (loop ends at the cap, ~line 64/103); empty turn -> `if not resp.tool_calls: transcript.stop_reason = "no_tool_call"; ... break` (~line 73); error -> wrapping `try/except Exception` sets `stop_reason = "error"` and exits (~line 110); submit -> `if call.name == "submit": ... submitted = True` then `if submitted: break` (~line 91-99). max_steps default 20 at types.py:118, read by the loop. All four triggers actually break/stop the loop.
spec_features.notes: All four termination conditions are wired and enforced. The cap is a turn cap, not a wall-clock/token deadline (no time/token threshold is compared).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The loop terminates on `submit`, on an error, or when `max_steps` is exceeded. Everything is recorded into a `Transcript`.

spec_features.spec_quote: `submit` is a first-class tool (rather than an out-of-band stop) so that "the agent declared it was done
spec_features.evidence: submit is a real registered tool in build_tool_registry (sandbox.py:181-189) with schema name 'submit' and a callable tool_submit (sandbox.py:126). The agent loop dispatches it like any tool and honors it as a stop: `if call.name == "submit": transcript.stop_reason = "submitted"; ... submitted = True` then `break` (agent.py ~line 91-99). So the agent can voluntarily end the episode via the tool, and it is honored.
spec_features.notes: tool_submit body is a sentinel ('Submission received.'); actual stop handling is in the agent loop, which is wired and works.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: submit with an honest summary of the final state, including whether the task's checks pass.
